newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open easier in quiet dealings.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open easier in quiet dealings.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened softer in quiet trading on Thursday as investors paused after a recent rally, worried that a weakening currency could spur a Bank of Canada interest rate increase.

"Certainly linger expectations of a Bank of Canada rate hike ... is keeping investors on the sidelines," said one money market analyst at a major bank. The dollar firmed slightly overnight to C$1.3809 (US$0.7242) from C$1.3823 (US$0.7234) but has slipped from last month's strength.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded to yield 3.34 percent from 3.33 percent at Tuesday's close.
One trader said that investors were selling some holdings to take profits after Tuesday's rally on bullish economic commentary by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

The trader added that unexpectedly strong U.S. initial claims for the week ended July 19 had increased U.S. rate hike concerns among investors. The Labor Department reported new claims for state unemployment insurance fell to 299,000, its lowest level in nearly a year, against a revised 341,000 in the previous week, .
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill traded to yield 3.70 percent from 3.69 percent on Wednesday.
The one-year when-issued T-bill eased to yield 4.20 percent from 4.16 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.30-3.35 percent, edging toward the top of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
